title: Frame-exact scroll scrub of one encoded clip with WebCodecs
summary: One clip packed as its encoded chunks, a JSON manifest of every frame's offset, length, time and type, and a four-byte pointer to the manifest: one fetch, no demuxer; WebCodecs decodes exactly the frame the scroll names, from the keyframe at or before it on a jump (ten at most), straight on from the decoder's own position when the target is ahead in the same group, one decode for the next frame; requests made while a seek decodes wait and only the newest runs (119 requests, 11 decodes); frames decoded on the way are kept as bitmaps, so scrubbing back is free; every `VideoFrame` closed; a 1 s watchdog; H.264, then VP9, then VP8; the demo encodes its film on load and measures it against WebP stills; frames drawn directly without WebCodecs; one still under reduced motion
variants: One packed file and WebCodecs (this, default)
An image sequence of stills (image-sequence-scrub): simplest, several times heavier
`<video>` with `currentTime`: lightest to build, not frame-exact under a fast scroll
